correctness.rationale: For q=λ∈[3/5,1] the reduced half-square has only taps −2 through 2. For x>0 and interior frequency the imaginary part has the sign of A1+2A2 cos θ; A2≥0 and A1−2A2=q∫Hq is strictly positive. The first pair of terms of Hq is nonincreasing, the second pair nondecreasing, and the endpoint Hq(1/2)=(5q−3)/2 is nonnegative. At q=3/5, Hq is positive near 0, enough for strict positivity of every integral to x>0. At x=0 the real polynomial is minimized at cos θ=−1 and its two scale branches are strictly positive; at ν=0 the central tap is positive. For ν=1/2 the absolutely convergent half-integer Fourier series gives S_q=(2q−1)²S_{q/(2q−1)}. For the rescaled parameter μ∈[1,3], the two- or three-tap formulas are positive for x<1/2 and vanish at x=1/2. For q below threshold in (3/7,3/5), μ=1/|2−1/q|>3 gives the stated compact-support gap; q=1/2 gives an identically zero half-frequency fiber. Reflection and conjugation handle the full half-open square. This is a uniform proof, not a grid inference. The supplied finite checker was inspected, not executed.

No new zero-set claim at other frequencies survives there.
